# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

**Thesis [L4].** Christ was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, with no man's seed involved. Mary was his only human parent. Joseph was his father only by supposition and by legal marriage, not by begetting. I rest this on the KJV text and on the Greek and Hebrew words that stand behind it.

## 1. Matthew's genealogy breaks its own pattern at the last link

**[L1]** Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob; and Jacob begat Judas and his brethren". The pattern is "A begat B", father to son.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."

**[L2]** The verb "begat" is gennaō (G1080, to beget, to bring forth). In verse 16 the verb changes to the passive, "was born" (egennēthē), and "of whom" is ex hēs (G1537 ek, out of, with the relative pronoun in the feminine singular). The one who is "out of" is the woman, Mary. Joseph is called "the husband of Mary" (ho anēr Marias, G435 anēr, man or husband), not the one who begat.

**[L3]** Matthew 1:18 gives the reason for the shift: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L4]** The line of "begat" ends at Joseph, and the child is "born" of Mary alone. Matthew 1:16 and the feminine ex hēs, with the pattern of 1:2, show that the text withholds the verb of fathering from Joseph.

## 2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost", before Joseph and Mary came together

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Before they came together" is prin ē synelthein autous (G4281 prin, before; G4905 synerchomai, to come together). The conception is dated before any union. "Of the Holy Ghost" is ek pneumatos hagiou (G1537 ek, out of; G4151 pneuma, spirit; G40 hagios, holy). The source of the conception is named.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."

**[L2]** "Conceived" is gennēthen (G1080), the same verb family Matthew used for every father in 1:2-16. Here the begetting is placed "in her" (en autē) and "of the Holy Ghost" (ek pneumatos hagiou).

**[L3]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." Here epelthō (G1904, to come upon) and episkiazō (G1982, to overshadow) name the divine act. "Therefore" is dio kai (G1352, wherefore also), which makes this act the reason for the title "Son of God". "Of thee" (ek sou) names the woman as the only human source.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 name the Holy Ghost as the source of the conception, and Luke 1:35 names the same act as the cause of the title "Son of God". The source is therefore not a man's seed.

## 3. Mary was a virgin, and Joseph "knew her not" until the birth

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"

**[L2]** "I know not" is ou ginōskō (G1097, to know), and "a man" is andra (G435). Ginōskō is the word for marital intercourse.

**[L3]** Genesis 4:1: "And Adam knew Eve his wife; and she conceived". The Hebrew yada (H3045, to know) is used the same way. Mary's question therefore asks how conception can happen without such knowing.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".

**[L2]** The same ginōskō appears, and "till" is heōs (G2193, until). Joseph did not know her through the whole span of the conception and birth.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."

**[L2]** "Put her away" is apolysai (G630, to release, to dismiss). Joseph resolves to dismiss her only because he knows the child is not his, and the angel's word in 1:20 turns him from that course.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:23: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son, and they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us."

**[L3]** Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The Hebrew behind the KJV's "virgin" is ha-almah (H5959). The KJV renders the same word "virgin" in Genesis 24:43: "when the virgin cometh forth to draw water". Of that same person Genesis 24:16 says "a virgin, neither had any man known her". Matthew 1:23 names the fulfilment, and in Greek the word is parthenos (G3933, virgin).

**[L4]** Luke 1:34, Matthew 1:25 and 1:19 all describe the absence of any marital union with a man, and Matthew 1:23 with Isaiah 7:14 describes the child as born to a virgin. A virgin conceiving, and a husband who does not know her until the birth, exclude a human father.

## 4. "Father" said of Joseph is supposition or legal standing, not begetting

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

**[L2]** "As was supposed" is hōs enomizeto (G3543 nomizō, to deem, to suppose). The text itself marks the sonship as a supposition.

**[L3]** Luke 2:49 gives the child's own correction of "thy father" in Luke 2:48: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?" Luke 2:48 reads: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". The child redirects the title "father" away from Joseph. The crowd's words in John 6:42, "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?", are what people said. They are not the narrator's testimony, and Luke 3:23 shows how the narrator qualifies that supposition.

**[L4]** The KJV narrators qualify the "son of Joseph" language with "as was supposed" (Luke 3:23). The child himself claims another Father in Luke 2:49. The sayings of Luke 2:48 and John 6:42 are therefore what was supposed and said, not biological testimony.

## 5. Davidic descent does not require a human father

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh". The verb is "made" (ginomai, G1096, to become), not "begotten".

**[L3]** Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman, made under the law". The woman is the human source. Luke 1:32 says "the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David", and Luke 1:31 says "thou shalt conceive in thy womb". The flesh descends from David through the woman, Mary.

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4 locate the human, fleshly descent in the woman. Davidic descent therefore does not depend on a human male begetter.

---

DECLARED CHAIN

1. Matthew's pattern "begat" (gennaō, to beget) ends at Joseph, "the husband of Mary", and the child is "born" of her (ex hēs, out of whom, feminine): Matthew 1:2 and 1:16 [L1], gennaō and ex hēs [L2], with Matthew 1:18 [L3].
2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost" (ek pneumatos hagiou, out of the Holy Spirit) and before Joseph and Mary came together, and the same act is the reason for the title "Son of God": Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], prin ē synelthein and gennēthen [L2], with Luke 1:35 [L3].
3. Mary was a virgin, and Joseph "knew her not" until the birth, so no marital union with a man took place: Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25 [L1], ginōskō and parthenos [L2], with Genesis 4:1 and Isaiah 7:14 [L3].
4. "Father" said of Joseph is supposition or legal standing, not begetting: Luke 3:23 [L1], nomizō (to suppose) [L2], with Luke 2:49 and John 6:42 [L3].
5. Christ had no human biological father: he was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, so Mary was his only human parent.

# Round 2: Defender's answer (revised)

## A. The question: how is it evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda?

**[L1]** Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood."

**[L2]** "Evident" is prodēlos (G4271, plain before all men, obvious). "Sprang" is anatellō (G393, to arise, to rise up). The verse states a plain rising out of the tribe, in the verb of arising.

**[L1]** Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers".

**[L2]** "Declared their pedigrees" is yalad (H3205, to beget, and also "to show lineage; declare pedigrees"). The law's counting is a declaration of lineage by the house.

**[L1]** Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David". Matthew 1:21: "And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS". Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife". Matthew 1:25: "he called his name JESUS".

**[L3]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

**[L4]** The house Numbers 1:18 counts is Joseph's, and Luke 2:4 gives Joseph that house. Joseph took Mary (Matthew 1:24) and gave the child his name (Matthew 1:21, 1:25), so the child stands in that house by taking and naming. Luke 3:23 says "son of Joseph" was reckoned "as was supposed". The fleshly seed of David is carried by the woman (see B, Premise 1). So the tribe is evident by the house's reckoning, and the flesh is David's through Mary.

## B. Answers to the challenger's chain

### C1 (the loins)

**[L1]** Acts 2:30: "that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ". Hebrews 7:5: "though they come out of the loins of Abraham".

**[L2]** Osphys (G3751) is "the loin... procreative power".

**[L3]** Hebrews 7:10: "For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him." Levi is said to be "in the loins" of Abraham, the ancestor of several generations, and the sons of Levi in Hebrews 7:5 are said to "come out of the loins of Abraham". 2 Samuel 7:12 says the seed "shall proceed out of thy bowels", which is said of David's whole line.

**[L4]** Hebrews 7:5 and 7:10 use "the loins" of a remote ancestor for descendants separated by many generations. Acts 2:30 therefore measures Christ's descent from David on the same pattern. The flesh is David's through the line, and Luke 1:35 states which body bore him: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". Together with Romans 1:3, "made of the seed of David according to the flesh", the chain runs from David's seed to Mary's body.

**[L1]** Hebrews 2:17: "in all things it behoved him to be made like unto [his] brethren".

**[L3]** Hebrews 4:15: "but was in all points tempted like as we are, yet without sin". The same epistle states the likeness of 2:17 with an exception, "yet without sin". Hebrews 2:16 reads "he took on [him] the seed of Abraham", and its margin gives "taketh hold". The verb names a taking hold of the seed of Abraham.

### C2 (the line is delivered to Joseph)

**[L1]** Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus".

**[L2]** The line of gennaō (G1080, to beget) ends at Joseph. The next clause changes to the passive, and "of whom" is feminine. The challenger agrees that ex hēs names the one who bore.

**[L3]** Luke 1:13: "thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son". Matthew 1:21: "she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS".

**[L4]** To Zacharias the angel says "shall bear thee a son", with the son borne to the husband. To Joseph the angel says "she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call". Joseph's part in Matthew 1:21 is the calling. The passage the challenger offers for Matthew 1:16 therefore shows a difference between the two cases.

### C3 (the father named by mother and narrator)

**[L1]** Luke 2:48: "thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing". Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my Father's business?"

**Correction.** In my opening I wrote "father's" in lower case. The KJV prints "Father's". I withdraw the lower-case form and stand on the KJV's capital.

**[L1]** Luke 1:34: "How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?" Luke 2:33: "And Joseph and his mother marvelled at those things which were spoken of him." Luke 2:43: "Joseph and his mother knew not of it".

**[L3]** Mark 6:3: "Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary".

**[L4]** Mary's "thy father" in Luke 2:48 is the household title she gave her husband. The child answers her at once with "my Father's" (Luke 2:49). The narrator writes "Joseph and his mother" in his own voice (2:33, 2:43), and Luke 3:23 qualifies "son of Joseph" with "as was supposed". "Parents" in 2:27 and 2:41 names the two who had charge of him.

### C4 ("of the Holy Ghost")

**[L1]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]".

**[L2]** Gennēthen (G1080) is the verb of begetting, with the margin's "begotten". The text sets it "in her" and "of" (ek, out of) the Holy Ghost in one clause. Matthew 1:2-16 had set that verb in each father.

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "she was found with child of the Holy Ghost".

**[L4]** The angel answers Joseph's "fear not" with "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost". The angel gives the source of the conception as the reason, so it is the ground for the taking.

**[L1]** Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."

**[L2]** Epelthō (G1904, to come upon), episkiazō (G1982, to overshadow), dynamis (G1411, power), pōs (G4459, how, by what means). Verse 35 is the answer to Mary's "How shall this be".

**[L3]** Acts 1:8: "after that the Holy Ghost is come upon you". 1 Samuel 16:13: "the Spirit of the LORD came upon David".

**[L4]** In Acts 1:8 and 1 Samuel 16:13 the persons already live, and the coming upon is for witness and anointing. In Luke 1:35 the coming upon answers a question about conception, and its outcome is "that holy thing which shall be born of thee". The same verbs put to a different question and a different outcome do not carry the same meaning. "Therefore also" follows the conception-act inside verse 35.

**[L1]** Romans 1:3-4: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; And declared [to be] the Son of God with power... by the resurrection from the dead." Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman".

**[L4]** Romans 1:3 calls the one "made" of David's seed "his Son", so the Son is the subject before he is made. Galatians 4:4 has the same order: "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman".

**[L1]** 1 Chronicles 28:6: "I have chosen him [to be] my son, and I will be his father".

**[L3]** Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]".

**[L4]** 1 Chronicles 28:6 states the ground of Solomon's sonship as "I have chosen him", a verb of selecting. Matthew 1:20 states the ground of Christ's conception as "is of the Holy Ghost", with the margin's "begotten". The first row carries the verb of choice and the second carries the verb of begetting. They are not the same shape.

**[L1]** John 1:13: "Which were born, not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God."

**[L2]** Ek (G1537, out of) governs both "of blood" and "of God".

**[L4]** John 1:13 states "not of blood, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God". Where the birth is "of God", the verse sets that origin in the place of blood and the will of man with "not... but". That verse speaks of believers' second birth. What it shows is how ek theou ("of God") works: it names the origin and replaces the human causes. Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:34 are the rows that apply this to the conception of Christ. I rest C4 on Matthew 1:20 and Luke 1:35, with John 1:13 as the pattern of the preposition.

### C5 (the union)

**[L1]** Matthew 1:18: "before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost". Matthew 1:25: "knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son".

**[L2]** Synerchomai (G4905) is "to cohabit (conjugally)". Ginōskō (G1097, to know) is the marital word of Genesis 4:1.

**[L4]** Matthew 1:18 states that she was found with child "before they came together", and Matthew 1:25 states "knew her not till" the birth. The rows that speak of knowing and of coming together both put the conception before any union. C5's step, "Joseph knew Mary his wife within the espousal", is therefore contrary to the rows.

## C. The unsupported-L4 premises

**Premise 1 (Mary of the house of David).**

**[L1]** Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh". Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee".

**[L2]** Sarx (G4561, flesh) is the body, "the means of kindred".

**[L4]** The body is "born of thee" (Luke 1:35), and that body is "of the seed of David according to the flesh" (Romans 1:3). Mary is therefore the one through whom David's seed comes. The challenger's rows are Luke 1:36, "thy cousin Elisabeth", and Luke 1:5, "daughters of Aaron". They give Elisabeth's line as Aaron's. Mary's descent from David rests on the chain above. I claim no verse that states Mary's tribe.

**Premise 2 (Matthew 1:19, narrowed).**

**[L1]** Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just [man]... was minded to put her away privily." Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost".

**[L4]** I narrow my wording. I rest on the angel's stated reason in Matthew 1:20, which answers Joseph's fear with the source of the conception, the Holy Ghost.

**Premise 3 (Galatians 4:4 and Romans 1:3).**

I grant that "born of a woman" (Job 14:1) and "born of women" (Matthew 11:11) are said of men who had fathers. I do not rest the exclusion of a father on Galatians 4:4. The exclusion rests on Matthew 1:18, 1:20 and Luke 1:34-35. Galatians 4:4 supplies "God sent forth his Son, made of a woman".

**Premise 4 (Luke 1:35).** Answered under C4: Luke 1:34, "How shall this be", is answered by Luke 1:35, "therefore also".

## D. The sign of Isaiah 7:14

**[L1]** Isaiah 8:3: "I went unto the prophetess; and she conceived, and bare a son. Then said the LORD to me, Call his name Mahershalalhashbaz." Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel."

**[L4]** The son of 8:3 is named Mahershalalhashbaz, and the child of 7:14 is named Immanuel. The woman of 7:14 is "a virgin", and the woman of 8:3 is "the prophetess". Different names and different women make these two rows two events. Matthew 1:22 says "all this was done, that it might be fulfilled", and what "was done" in Matthew is the birth of 1:18-25, "before they came together".

## E. Luke 3:23

**[L1]** Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph".

**[L2]** Hōs (G5613, as) marks what is reckoned, and nomizō (G3543, to deem) is the verb. Acts 16:13 gives "where prayer was wont to be made", a place held to be a place of prayer.

**[L4]** In both verses the verb states what was held. In Luke 3:23 the thing held is "the son of Joseph", held "as was supposed", and Luke 1:34-35 gives the facts it is set against.

DECLARED CHAIN (restated)

1. Matthew's "begat" (gennaō, to beget) ends at Joseph, "the husband of Mary", and the child is "of whom was born": Matthew 1:2 and 1:16 [L1], ex hēs [L2], with Luke 1:13 and Matthew 1:21 [L3].
2. The conception was "of the Holy Ghost", before they came together, and the angel gives it as the ground of Joseph's "fear not": Matthew 1:18 and 1:20 [L1], gennēthen and synerchomai [L2], with Luke 1:35 [L3].
3. Mary says "I know not a man", and Joseph "knew her not till" the birth: Luke 1:34 and Matthew 1:25 [L1], ginōskō [L2], with Genesis 4:1 and Isaiah 7:14 [L3].
4. "Son of Joseph" is "as was supposed", and the child answers "thy father" with "my Father's": Luke 3:23 and Luke 2:49 [L1], nomizō [L2], with Luke 2:48 [L3].
5. Christ had no human biological father: he was conceived in Mary by the Holy Ghost, so Mary was his only human parent.

DEFENDER (standard reading) -- ROUND 3, LINK ROUND

**LINK 5 [premise 1]: SUPPORTED**

The link is an inference from rows, not a stated genealogy of Mary. Its footing:

- [L1] Luke 1:35: "that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God." The child's body is born of Mary. Luke 1:31 adds: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son."
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh."
- [L3] Galatians 4:4: "made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L2] ginomai (G1096, to become, to be made) stands in Romans 1:3 and in Galatians 4:4. [L2] sarx (G4561, flesh, "the means of kindred") stands in Romans 1:3.
- [L4] The one verb "made" is said of David's seed in Romans 1:3 and of a woman in Galatians 4:4. The flesh Luke 1:35 gives as "born of thee" is the flesh Romans 1:3 calls David's seed. So David's seed reaches the child through the woman who bore him, and Mary's body is the way it reaches him.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Luke 1:27 and Luke 2:4.** Press: the house of David is given to Joseph by name. I grant it. Luke 2:4 says "because he was of the house and lineage of David." That is the house in which the child is counted by Joseph's taking (Matthew 1:20, 24, 25). It does not set aside the flesh through Mary shown above.
- **Luke 1:36 and Luke 1:5.** Press: the kinswoman is of Aaron's daughters. [L2] syngenēs (G4773, a relative by blood) stands in Luke 1:36. It gives a blood tie between Mary and Elisabeth. [L3] Matthew 1:3, "Judas begat Phares and Zara of Thamar," shows a line of descent running through a woman. A tie to Aaron through a woman is therefore consistent with David's seed in the same woman's line.
- **Acts 2:30 and Hebrews 7:10.** [L2] osphys (G3751, loin, procreative power) stands in Acts 2:30. [L2] patēr (G3962, father, "near or more remote") stands in Hebrews 7:10. Hebrews 7:5 says "though they come out of the loins of Abraham," which is descent of persons from an ancestor. Acts 2:30 pairs "the fruit of his loins" with "according to the flesh." Luke 1:35 gives that flesh as "born of thee." [L4] The rows fix David's procreative power as the source. They name Mary's body as the way it reaches the child.
- **Romans 1:3 with 2 Samuel 7:12.** 2 Samuel 7:12 says "thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels." It fixes the source in David. Romans 1:3 says "made of the seed of David," and Galatians 4:4 says "made of a woman." Both are carried by the chain above.

**LINK 5 [premise 2]: SUPPORTED**

Footing:

- [L1] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers, according to the number of the names."
- [L2] yalad (H3205) here means to declare pedigrees. [L2] miçpâr (H4557, number) and shem (H8034, name) stand in the same verse.
- [L4] The reckoning the verse describes is a counting by names within a house. The same law counts Christ in David's house by his name and by Joseph's taking.
- [L1] Matthew 1:21: "thou shalt call his name JESUS."
- [L1] Matthew 1:24: "took unto him his wife."
- [L1] Luke 2:4: "because he was of the house and lineage of David."
- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda." [L2] prodēlos (G4271, plain before all men) points to a public reckoning. That reckoning is Numbers 1:18's, by names and houses.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Numbers 1:18 with yalad.** I grant that the verse declares pedigrees by the house of the fathers. The verse's own measure is "the number of the names." Christ is counted by name in Joseph's house.
- **Ezra 2:59.** The verse says "they could not shew their father's house, and their seed." What fails there is a showing, a register. A register is the reckoning I keep. The flesh limb rests on Luke 1:35 with Romans 1:3 and Galatians 4:4, shown above.
- **Hebrews 7:14 with Numbers 1:2.** The tribe is "evident." Numbers 1:2 says the reckoning is "after their families, by the house of their fathers, with the number of [their] names." The child is in that house by taking and naming.
- **Luke 2:4 with Luke 1:27.** I grant that Joseph's house is David's. That is the house in which the child is counted.

**LINK 1: SUPPORTED**

Footing:

- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L3] Matthew 1:2: "Abraham begat Isaac; and Isaac begat Jacob." Every earlier link in the chain is "X begat Y."
- [L2] gennaō (G1080) means "to procreate (properly, of the father, but by extension of the mother)." In Matthew 1:16 the active "begat" ends at Joseph, who is titled "the husband of Mary." The passive "was born" follows with the feminine "of whom."
- [L4] The chain's active begetting verb stops at Joseph with the title "husband." The bearing is given to the woman. This withholds the verb of fathering from Joseph in the text.

Answers to the pressed witnesses:

- **Luke 1:13 and Matthew 1:21 on calling.** Luke 1:13 says "shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John." Matthew 1:21 says "she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS." Calling the name is not confined to fathers:
  - Luke 1:31 gives the calling to Mary: "thou shalt conceive in thy womb, and bring forth a son, and shalt call his name JESUS."
  - Genesis 4:25 gives it to a mother: "she bare a son, and called his name Seth."
  - [L2] kaleō (G2564, to call) is the verb in each verse. So Matthew 1:25, "he called his name JESUS," is an act of naming, which the rows give to either parent.
- **Matthew 1:20.** The press: the Davidic sonship is delivered to Joseph. The address is "Joseph, thou son of David." The sentence continues: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]." [L2] huios (G5207, son) is used "of immediate, remote or figuratively, kinship." The margin gives the verb gennaō (G1080) as "begotten." The begetting named in this sentence is "of the Holy Ghost." The title "son of David" names the house into which Joseph is told to receive her ("take unto thee Mary thy wife"). Matthew 1:1 gives the child "the son of David." Matthew 1:20 supplies the house, not a second begetter.
- **Matthew 1:25.** "He called his name JESUS" is Joseph's naming, answered above under calling.

**LINK 2: SUPPORTED**

Footing:

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]."
- [L2] gennaō (G1080) is "to procreate." The Holy Ghost is named as source of what is begotten.
